title: In the City
description: Ten short stories about everyday life in an American city: the bank, the post office, finding the way, neighbors, the library, a phone store, the airport, a film night, a vote on a new park and the morning train.

lessons.title: A Bank Account for Tom
lessons.summary: Maria and her son, Tom, go to the bank and open an account so Tom can save his money.
lessons.text:
Maria lives in the city with her son, Tom. Tom is 12 years old. He has $80. He wants to save his money. Maria says, "You can save your money in a bank. You can open a bank account."

On Saturday, Maria and her son go to the bank. The bank is near their house. There are many people in the bank. Maria and Tom wait for half an hour.

Then a woman says, "Hi. How can I help you?"

Maria answers, "My son wants to open an account. Is it possible?"

"Yes, it is possible," the woman answers. "The process is easy. It takes about half an hour."

First, the woman asks Tom some questions: "What is your name? Where do you live? How old are you?" Tom answers every question. Then the woman asks Maria some questions. Maria answers too.

"Wait a moment, please," the woman says. She works on her computer for a moment. Then she gives Tom a small card. "This is your bank card. Now you have an account."

Tom puts his $80 in the account.

"Can I save more money?" Tom asks.

"Yes," the woman answers. "You can put money in your account every week. It is easy."

On the way home, Tom says, "The process is really easy. I want to save $5 every week."

Maria thinks it is a good idea. She is happy for her son.

Questions:
Who is Tom?
Tom is Maria's son.
What does Tom want to do with his money?
He wants to save his money.
How long do Maria and Tom wait in the bank?
They wait for half an hour.
What does Maria ask the woman?
She asks, "My son wants to open an account. Is it possible?"
Is the process hard?
No, the process is easy.
How much does Tom want to save every week?
He wants to save $5 every week.

lessons.title: A Present for Sam
lessons.summary: Leo sends a birthday present and a short note to his friend in Canada from the post office near his house.
lessons.text:
Leo has a good friend, Sam. Sam lives in Canada. In 2 weeks, it is Sam's birthday. Leo wants to send him a present.

Leo buys a present for Sam. It is a book about music. Sam loves music. Leo puts the book in a small red box. Then he writes a note. The note is short. Leo writes, "Happy birthday, Sam! Your friend, Leo."

Leo also puts a picture in the red box. It is a picture of Leo and Sam at school. In the picture, they are 10 years old.

The post office is near Leo's house. It is on the next street. Leo walks to the post office with the present. There are several people in line. Leo waits.

Then a man at the post office says, "Next, please."

"Hi. I want to send this present to Canada," Leo says.

"Canada? So this present is going to another country. It is international," the man says. "Please write the address here."

Leo writes the address on a form. The man looks at the present. "International service costs $25," he says. Leo pays.

"When can my friend expect the present?" Leo asks.

"International service takes several days," the man says. "Your friend can expect it in 6 or 7 days."

Leo is happy. Sam can expect the present in about a week. That is a week before his birthday.

Questions:
Where does Sam live?
Sam lives in Canada.
What is the present?
The present is a book about music.
What does Leo write?
He writes a short note.
What is in the picture?
In the picture, Leo and Sam are at school.
Where is the post office?
The post office is near Leo's house.
When can Sam expect the present?
He can expect the present in 6 or 7 days.

lessons.title: The Wrong Road
lessons.summary: Anna walks the wrong way to the City Art Center, and a police officer shows her the right road.
lessons.text:
Anna is new in the city. She loves art. Today she wants to go to the City Art Center. She does not have a car, so she walks.

The Art Center is south of Anna's house. But Anna does not know the city well. She walks north. She walks along a long road. She walks for half an hour. There is no art here. There are only houses and trees.

"I think this is the wrong road," Anna says.

Near the road, Anna sees a police car. A police officer is standing next to the car. Anna asks him for help.

"I want to go to the City Art Center. Is this the right road?"

"No, this is the wrong road," the police officer says. "You are walking north. The Art Center is south."

"Oh no! What can I do?"

"Turn around. Walk south along this road. Then take the third street on the left. The Art Center is on that street."

"The third street on the left. Thank you!"

Anna turns around. Now she walks south along the road. She counts the streets: the first street, the second street, the third street. She takes the third street on the left. There is the City Art Center!

Anna is tired, but she is happy. She looks at the art for 2 hours. Then she walks home. This time she takes the right road.

Questions:
What does Anna love?
Anna loves art.
Where does Anna want to go?
She wants to go to the City Art Center.
Which way does Anna walk first?
She walks north. It is the wrong road.
Who helps Anna?
A police officer helps Anna.
Where is the Art Center?
The Art Center is south, on the third street on the left.

lessons.title: The New Guy on Oak Street
lessons.summary: Kate hears her new neighbor Mark play songs every night, tells him she likes them and invites him to a party.
lessons.text:
Kate lives in a small house on Oak Street. A new guy lives in the house next to Kate's house. His name is Mark. Mark is young and nice.

Every night, Kate hears music. The music comes from Mark's house. Mark plays songs. Kate hears a new song every night. The songs sound pretty. Kate likes the sound very much.

One day, Kate meets Mark on the street.

"Hi, I'm Kate," she says. "I live in the house next to your house. I hear your songs every night."

"Oh, I'm sorry," Mark says. "Is that a problem?"

"No, no," Kate says. "Your songs sound very nice. They make me happy."

Now Mark is happy too. "Thank you! That is really nice."

"Do you know anyone else on the street?" Kate asks.

"No," Mark says. "I'm new here. I don't know anyone."

"Come to my house on Saturday," Kate says. "I'm having a small party. You can meet everyone else."

On Saturday, Mark comes to the party. Kate's friends are there. Mark plays some songs for them. Everyone likes the sound.

"Your songs are really pretty," a woman says.

"Thank you," Mark says. "Does anyone else want to play?"

Nobody else wants to play. Everyone wants to hear Mark. So Mark plays one more song.

Mark is very happy. Now he knows several people on Oak Street. And every night, Kate hears a new song.

Questions:
Who is Mark?
Mark is the new guy in the house next to Kate's house.
What does Kate hear every night?
She hears Mark's songs.
How do the songs sound?
The songs sound nice and pretty.
Does Mark know anyone on the street?
No, he doesn't know anyone.
What does Mark do at the party?
He plays some songs.

lessons.title: Emma Joins the Library
lessons.summary: Emma joins the county library for a school project on the history of her city and learns its rules.
lessons.text:
Emma is a student. She has a school project. Her project is about the history of her city. For her project, she needs to do some research.

Emma's mother says, "The county library is a good source of information. It has many books about the history of our county."

So on Saturday, Emma goes to the county library. She wants to join the library. A man works there. Emma asks him, "Can I join the library?"

"Yes, of course," the man says. "It is free, and it is easy to join." He gives Emma a card. "Now you can take books home. But there are some rules."

"What are the rules?" Emma asks.

"Rule 1: there is a limit. The limit is 5 books. Rule 2: the books are due in 3 weeks. Please bring them back on the due date."

"I understand," Emma says.

Emma looks for books for her research. She finds a big book with a green cover. On the cover, there is an old picture of the city. The book is about the history of the county. It is a very good source for her project.

She finds 3 more books. They have old covers, but they are good sources too. Now Emma has 4 books. The limit is 5, so that is fine.

Emma reads the books at home. Every day, she does some research. Then she writes her project. The books are due on Friday. On Thursday, she brings them back. Emma follows the rules.

Questions:
What is Emma's project about?
Her project is about the history of her city.
Where does Emma go on Saturday?
She goes to the county library.
What is the limit?
The limit is 5 books.
When are the books due?
The books are due in 3 weeks.
What is on the cover of the big book?
There is an old picture of the city on the cover.

lessons.title: A New Phone
lessons.summary: Jack's phone is very old, so he goes to a phone store and buys a new one with good features.
lessons.text:
Jack has a very old phone. It doesn't work well. Jack wants a new phone. On Saturday, he goes to a phone store on Main Street. The store sells phones.

A young man works at the store. "Hi! Can I help you?"

"Yeah," Jack says. "I need a new phone. My phone is really old."

"Okay. We sell a lot of phones. What do you use your phone for?"

"For example, I take a lot of pictures. And I use social media every day."

"Okay. Look at this phone. It has a lot of good features. For example, it takes very good pictures. It is great for social media too."

"How much is it?"

"It is $600."

"Oh. That is a lot of money," Jack says.

"Yeah, it is a lot. But here is another phone. It is $300. It has most of the same features."

"Okay. I use a lot of data. Is that a problem?"

"No, it isn't. We also sell data plans. Our big data plan has a lot of data for a good price."

"And my old pictures? I won't lose them?"

"No, you won't lose anything. I can move your pictures and data to the new phone. It won't take long."

"Great. I want the $300 phone and the big data plan."

Jack pays. The young man moves the pictures and data to the new phone. It isn't hard.

Now Jack has a new phone. He takes a picture of Main Street. He puts it on social media.

Questions:
What is the problem with Jack's phone?
Jack's phone is very old, and it doesn't work well.
What does the store sell?
The store sells phones.
What does Jack use his phone for?
For example, he takes a lot of pictures and uses social media.
Which phone does Jack buy?
He buys the $300 phone.
Will Jack lose his old pictures?
No, he won't lose his old pictures.

lessons.title: At the Airport
lessons.summary: Lucy goes to the airport to pick up her old friend Ana, who comes back from London to the city where she was born.
lessons.text:
Lucy is at the airport. Her old friend Ana is coming from London. Ana was born in this city, but now she lives in London. Lucy wants to pick her up.

Ana's plane is in the air now. Lucy looks up. She sees a plane in the air. It is approaching the city. It comes down. Then it lands.

"That is probably Ana's plane," Lucy thinks.

Lucy goes to baggage claim. Many people come there. They claim their bags and go. Lucy waits and waits. People appear one by one. But Ana does not appear.

"She is probably still in line," Lucy thinks. "She can appear at any moment."

Soon Ana appears. She claims a big red bag and comes to Lucy.

"Lucy!"

"Ana! It is so good to see you!"

They walk to the car. Soon they are on the road to the city. They are approaching the city center.

Ana looks at the streets. "I was born in this city," she says. "I was born on South Road. Can we drive along South Road? I want to see my old house."

"Of course," Lucy says. "But first, we can eat something. You probably want some food."

"Yes, I do," Ana says. "Thank you for picking me up."

Soon they are at a nice place on South Road. They eat and talk for a long time.

Questions:
Who is Lucy waiting for?
Lucy is waiting for her old friend Ana.
Where was Ana born?
Ana was born in this city, on South Road.
What is the plane doing?
The plane is approaching the city. Then it lands.
What do people do at baggage claim?
They claim their bags.
Does Ana appear soon?
Yes, soon Ana appears. She claims a big red bag.

lessons.title: Film Night
lessons.summary: Sara and her friend Ben go to a free film night at the community center and watch an action film.
lessons.text:
On Friday night, the community center has a special film night. The film is free. Sara and her friend Ben want to go.

"What is the film?" Ben asks.

"It is an action film," Sara says. "The star is Chris Lane. He is the star of a television series too."

"Oh, I know him! I watch his television series every week. He is a great star."

The film begins at 7. Sara and Ben are at the community center at 6:30. They buy drinks. Ben gets a cold drink. Sara gets a hot drink.

Many people come. The room is full. At 7, the film begins.

The film is about a police officer in a big city. There is a lot of action. Cars drive fast. People run in the streets. Chris Lane is the police officer. He helps a little girl and her family. He has a big heart.

Ben drinks his cold drink and watches the action. Sara likes the film, but she thinks there is a bit too much action.

The film ends at 9. "What do you think of the film?" Ben asks.

"I like it," Sara says. "It is a bit long, and there is a bit too much action. But I like the star. In the film, he has a big heart. He helps everyone."

"Next Friday, the center has another special night," Ben says. "The film is with Chris Lane too. Do you want to come?"

"Yes!" Sara says. "And we can get drinks again."

Questions:
What does the community center have on Friday night?
It has a special film night.
Who is the star of the film?
The star is Chris Lane.
When does the film begin?
The film begins at 7.
What drinks do Sara and Ben get?
Ben gets a cold drink. Sara gets a hot drink.
What does Sara think about the action?
She thinks there is a bit too much action.

lessons.title: A Field for the Kids
lessons.summary: The people on David's street vote on the future of an old field, and the city makes it a place for kids to play.
lessons.text:
David lives on Pine Street. From his house, he has a view of an old field. No one uses the field. No one cuts the grass there, and it is very high.

The kids on Pine Street play in the street. It is not a good place to play. The kids hit the ball very hard, and the ball can hit a car. David thinks, "The kids need a better place to play."

The city has a plan for the old field. There are two ideas for the site. The first idea is a big store. The second idea is a park with a field for the kids. The city asks the people to vote. "Come and vote on the future of the site," the city says.

David reads about the development. He likes the second idea. A park is good for the future of the kids. On Saturday, David goes to vote. Many people from Pine Street vote too.

The next week, the city gives the final result. In the final vote, 520 people vote for the park, and 210 people vote for the store. The second idea wins.

Soon the development begins. The city cuts the high grass. It makes a new field for the kids.

Now the kids play on the new field, not in the street. And David has a new view from his house: kids playing on a field.

Questions:
What can David see from his house?
He has a view of an old field.
Where do the kids play?
They play in the street.
Why is the street not a good place to play?
The ball can hit a car.
What are the two ideas for the site?
A big store or a park with a field for the kids.
How many people vote for the park in the final vote?
520 people vote for the park.
What does the city cut?
It cuts the high grass.

lessons.title: The Morning Train
lessons.summary: Lisa takes the train to her new job every morning and makes a friend on the way.
lessons.text:
Lisa got a new position at a big company in the city 2 weeks ago. Now she takes the train to work every morning.

The train leaves at 7:30 in the morning. The ride is short. It takes almost half an hour. Lisa often reads a book on the way.

Every morning, Lisa sees the same people. There is an old man with a book. There is a young woman with a red phone. The young woman often sits near Lisa.

One morning, the young woman says, "Hi. Do you work in the city too?"

"Yes," Lisa says. "I have a new position at a big company. I got the position 2 weeks ago."

"That is great," the woman says. "My name is Jen. I work at the bank on Elm Street."

"Is that true? My company is on Elm Street too!"

"Then we can walk there together," Jen says.

The train comes to the city at almost 8. Lisa and Jen get off. They walk together. They walk past a small hotel. They walk past the post office. Then they are on Elm Street. The walk is short.

Now Lisa and Jen often talk in the morning. The ride feels short. Lisa was new in the city 2 weeks ago. She didn't know anyone. Now she has a friend. It is true: the morning train is a good place to meet people.

Questions:
What does Lisa have?
She has a new position at a big company.
When did Lisa get the position?
She got the position 2 weeks ago.
When does the train leave?
It leaves at 7:30 in the morning.
Is the ride long?
No, the ride is short. It takes almost half an hour.
What do Lisa and Jen walk past?
They walk past a small hotel and the post office.
What do Lisa and Jen often do in the morning?
They often talk.
